Thanks for the quick turnaround on PR #32966, @lexlian. Before this gets treated as resolved, I have a few doubts — the issue is still open and I'm not convinced the fix covers the original failure path:

1. **Which layer is actually fixed?** The report (and the duplicate-bot note on #32613) pins the root cause on the *OpenCode Go backend* relaying a list-type `messages.content` to a model that expects a string — i.e. server-side. PR #32966 adds a transform on the *opencode client* side. For setups that never touch the opencode client — e.g. `Claude Code → cc-switch local proxy → OpenCode Go → GLM-5.2` — would a client-side transform take effect at all? That's exactly the repro path, and it looks untouched.

2. **Scope vs. the actual error.** Per your description, the PR flattens *single-part tool-role* content for `FLATTEN_TOOL_CONTENT_PROVIDERS`. But the error is `messages[1].content.str`, and the repro is "send any text prompt" — no tool call involved. Wouldn't a plain user/assistant message with array content still trigger the same 400? Tool-result flattening alone doesn't seem to cover that.

3. **Has it been verified?** Was the fix tested against the original repro (cc-switch + OpenCode Go plan + glm-5.2, plain text prompt)? If it passes end-to-end now, confirming that on the issue before closing would help. If not, the server-side relay may be the real fix site.

Happy to share request/response captures from the cc-switch → OpenCode Go path if that helps localize it.

This issue appears to combine both of those pre-existing bugs into a single report. It may be worth closing this in favour of commenting on each of those issues, or linking them together.

Additional data point: In our case, model listing succeeded - models were fetched correctly after the OAuth flow. However, any inference call (actually sending a message) failed silently. This suggests the broken URL construction affects the inference endpoint specifically, not model discovery.

Workaround: Manually removing the `enterpriseUrl` field from `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` after the /connect flow resolved the issue completely - both model listing and inference worked afterwards.

Thanks for the pointer to #23896 — same underlying problem, but I'll keep this open to note the Web/Desktop difference.

My setup: **2560×1080 (21:9)** monitor, half-screen window (~1280px). Desktop keeps the sidebar fixed at this width. Web collapses it into a hamburger menu right at the Tailwind `xl` breakpoint.

I understand the Web UI needs to adapt to phones and tablets. Instead of a simple on/off toggle, perhaps the cleanest solution is a **configurable breakpoint width** — let users set the threshold at which the sidebar collapses. Set it to `0` to disable responsive collapse entirely (always fixed), or to `800` to keep the sidebar fixed on a half-screen laptop, or leave it at the default `1280`. This would cover both this issue and #23896 with one setting.

Additional evidence after restart on June 23, 2026:

A fresh debug bundle captured at `2026-06-23T09:10:25.725Z` shows that restarting OpenCode does not resolve the issue if the app restores the same problematic session/review state.

New debug bundle:
- `C:\Users\Administrator\Downloads\opencode-debug-20260623T091025.zip`
- Current run in manifest: `C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Roaming\ai.opencode.desktop\logs\20260623T090946`

What happened:
- App startup itself was normal.
- Shortly after startup, the renderer became unresponsive again.
- The unresponsive samples show the same call path as before:
  - `execEditLength`
  - `LineDiff.diffWithOptionsObj`
  - `diffLines`
  - `structuredPatch`
  - `createTwoFilesPatch`
  - `parseDiffFromFile`
  - `fileDiffFromContent`
  - `fileDiffFromPatch`
  - `resolveFileDiff`
  - SessionReview-related computations / collapsible open state

Log evidence from `...\20260623T090946\window.log`:
- `2026-06-23 17:10:18.818` renderer unresponsive
- `2026-06-23 17:10:25.716` unresponsive sample rooted in diff computation
- `2026-06-23 17:10:41.306` same stack again
- `2026-06-23 17:10:55.268` renderer responsive

`main.log` shows startup and sidecar/server initialization completed normally before the UI stall.

A temporary local workaround that proved the trigger:
I closed OpenCode and cleared only the local UI/session restore state for the affected workspace under:
- `C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Roaming\ai.opencode.desktop\opencode.workspace.D--ruoyi-vue.1ninrv3.dat`
- `C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Roaming\ai.opencode.desktop\opencode.global.dat`

Specifically, I removed the auto-restored session/review state and last project session pointer for `D:\ruoyi-vue-pro`, while keeping repo/db/account data intact.

After that, OpenCode started again in a fresh UI state (new log dir `20260623T092420`) and did not immediately reproduce the renderer-unresponsive diff stack.

This strongly suggests there are two coupled bugs:
1. Large deleted-file diff/review rendering can freeze the renderer.
2. Restarting the app can automatically restore the same problematic review/session state, causing the freeze to recur immediately after startup.

Hey, I hit this same bug on v1.15.7 and v1.17.9 with mimo-v2.5-free via OpenCode Zen.

My session had ~1,048,572 tokens (4 below the 1,048,576 limit). The next
request exceeded the limit and the provider returned a context-length error,
but it showed up as "Network connection lost" with no retry.

The error object looked like:
{"name":"UnknownError","data":{"message":"\"Network connection lost.\""}}

Sounds like the same classification gap — context overflow errors wrapped in
generic Error fall through to NamedError.Unknown instead of being caught as
ContextOverflowError. The retry logic in retry.ts never fires because it
only handles APIError.

Not sure if this is the same root cause as the 502 case you described, but
the symptom is identical: session dies with no recovery.

I saw this firsthand on v1.15.7. Was running a 100-step sequential thinking
review and the per-step latency went from ~6s to 100s+ by step 50. The
session eventually hung.

The reasoning-delta handler was the bottleneck — each small token addition
triggered V8 string flattening because the UI render loop reads the text
between writes.

Haven't tested the fix yet but the array accumulator approach makes sense.

Same thing on my end. Session had 937M cache read tokens but only ~41MB of
actual data. The cumulative counter was way out of sync with reality.

This made the context overflow from Bug #3 worse — the session thought it
was already over the limit when the actual context was still manageable.

I think I found one specific case of this. On v1.15.7 with mimo-v2.5-free,
my session hit the 1,048,576 token context limit and the provider returned
a context_length_exceeded error. But fromError() classified it as
NamedError.Unknown with message "Network connection lost." — which isn't
retryable and doesn't trigger compaction.

The fix would be to detect context overflow patterns in the Error catch-all
before it falls through to NamedError.Unknown. Something like checking for
/context|token|limit|exceed in the error message.

**Same error on 1.17.4, but via the _opposite_ branch — `differentModel === false` (same-model compaction)**

Confirming this still reproduces on **1.17.4** (Amazon Bedrock), but through a different path than the issue body describes. The current write-up only covers `differentModel === true`; the same-model case is also broken and I think it's worth documenting here.

**Repro:**
- Session model: `amazon-bedrock/claude-opus-4-8`, `xhigh` variant (extended thinking on).
- No `compaction` agent configured, so the compaction model resolves to the triggering message's model:
  ```ts
  const model = agent.model
    ? getModel(agent.model.providerID, agent.model.modelID)
    : getModel(userMessage.model.providerID, userMessage.model.modelID) // ← same as the session model
  ```
- `/compact` → 400 from Bedrock `converse-stream`:
  ```
  messages.35.content.1: `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the latest assistant
  message cannot be modified. These blocks must remain as they were in the original response.
  ```
- Retrying after switching the session model to `claude-sonnet-4-6` → **succeeds**.

**Why it fails on the same-model path:** because the compaction model == the model that produced the history, `differentModel === false`, so `toModelMessagesEffect` replays the stored reasoning parts as real `reasoning`/thinking blocks _with their original `bedrock.signature`_. The replayed `selected.head` ends on an assistant turn, so a thinking block lands in the "latest assistant message", and after the reorder/merge into Bedrock Converse format it's no longer the pristine first block (note the error points at `content.1`) → Anthropic rejects it.

**Why the model-switch retry succeeds (and a correction to the issue body):** in 1.17.4 the `differentModel === true` branch no longer strips just the signature — it downgrades the whole reasoning part to plain text:
```js
if (part.type === "reasoning") {
  if (differentModel) {
    if (part.text.trim().length > 0) parts.push({ type: "text", text: part.text })
    continue                                   // ← thinking block dropped entirely
  }
  parts.push({ type: "reasoning", text: part.text, providerMetadata: part.metadata })
}
```
So switching models flips `differentModel` to `true`, strips the thinking blocks, and sidesteps the error. The v1.16.2 mechanism in the description (differentModel=true keeping an *unsigned* thinking block) appears fixed, but the **`differentModel === false` / same-model case is still broken**.

This is more evidence that the proposed `stripReasoning: true` option for compaction is the right fix regardless of branch — reasoning content isn't needed to summarize the conversation, and stripping it unconditionally avoids both variants.

_(Confirmed by inspecting the shipped 1.17.4 build plus the stored session messages; the failing request had the thinking block at `content[1]` of the final assistant message, produced by the same Opus model used for compaction.)_

Same issue still reproduces on **v1.17.9** (Windows Desktop connecting to an opencode server running on Ubuntu Server on the same LAN).

**Scenario:** I have a repo with two git worktrees — `/home/user/dev/time-tracking` and `/home/user/dev/time-tracking-mobile`. When I select `time-tracking` in the Windows Desktop "Open Project" dialog, the app opens `time-tracking-mobile` instead. The opencode server's DB shows a single project entry with `time-tracking-mobile` as the primary path and `time-tracking` collapsed into `sandboxes`. Both resolve to the same `projectID`, so the Desktop client redirects to whichever worktree was first persisted instead of honoring the exact directory I selected.

This is not just a local Desktop issue — it also affects the **server-backed workflow** (Ubuntu server + Windows Desktop client), where the server stores a single project entry per git repo root and the client has no way to open a specific worktree as an independent project.

PR #16389 fixed session loss across worktrees, but the **project ID collision** that maps multiple worktrees to a single project entry remains. The project identity should incorporate the worktree path so each worktree can be opened and persisted as a distinct project, especially in server/client setups where path uniqueness is essential.
